title: Reminiscing in Tempo and the concert pieces
summary: Greer recalls recording the four-side piece for Duke's mother, written out; Duke wrote new works for Carnegie concerts.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Now, do you remember the recording? Do you remember working on a piece "Reminiscing in Tempo" that he dedicated to his mother? That long recording that was on four sides?
Yeah, I remember that. I made it.
But I mean, when you all went to record that, had the guys memorized the music? Or were they reading it?
No, when we recorded that, that was written out because it was so long. First time we recorded it. Well, eventually they memorized it.
Did you all play it in performance much?
Not -- we played in concerts. That was written strictly for concerts. You see, Duke wrote different numbers, every concert we played at Carnegie Hall, every year
